skill.name: system-environment-setup
skill.description: Configure repeatable development environments with Docker Compose, environment variable templates, dev containers, Makefile tasks, and Terraform examples.
skill.summary: Build consistent local and infrastructure setup templates for application teams.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, placeholder environment variables, and infrastructure examples. I found no prompt injection, executable malware, or data exfiltration intent, but the Docker Compose sample includes weak copyable database credentials.

remediation.issue: Weak default database credentials appear in the Docker Compose example.
remediation.suggestion: Use clearly non-deployable placeholders and instruct users to generate unique local passwords before starting shared services.

remediation.issue: Secret placeholders resemble real service credentials in environment examples.
remediation.suggestion: Mark all secret values as placeholders and recommend a secret manager for production deployments.

remediation.issue: Database and cache ports are exposed in local examples.
remediation.suggestion: Document that exposed ports are for local development and should be restricted or removed in shared environments.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Default Database Credentials in Example
semantic_findings.description: The Docker Compose example sets POSTGRES_USER to postgres and POSTGRES_PASSWORD to password. Users may copy these defaults into shared environments, creating an avoidable credential risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The weak credentials are present in the setup example and can be copied directly. The risk is contextual because the skill also says not to commit secrets.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time when local services, secrets, and infrastructure differ across machines. This skill creates repeatable setup templates for Docker, dev containers, and Terraform.
actual_capabilities: Drafts Docker Compose service layouts for web, database, cache, and reverse proxy services.
Creates environment variable templates with required application, database, cache, token, email, and API settings.
Provides VS Code dev container settings for container-based development workflows.
Defines Makefile commands for common install, test, Docker, migration, and cleanup tasks.
Sketches Terraform examples for AWS providers, VPCs, RDS, ECS, load balancers, and variables.
limitations: Examples require security review before production use.
The skill does not validate generated infrastructure against live cloud accounts.
Placeholder credentials must be replaced with managed secrets.
Generated commands assume Node.js, Docker Compose, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Terraform workflows.

use_cases.title: Create a New Project Environment
use_cases.description: Generate starter files for local services, environment variables, and repeatable developer commands.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Onboarding
use_cases.description: Document a shared setup that helps new contributors start services and install tools consistently.

use_cases.title: Prototype Cloud Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Prepare Terraform scaffolding for common AWS application resources before a production review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Local Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new service stack.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Docker Compose setup for a Node.js web app with PostgreSQL and Redis. Include required environment variables and simple run commands.

prompt_templates.title: Add Developer Tooling
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for repeatable contributor workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a dev container and Makefile for this project. Include install, test, lint, Docker, migration, and cleanup tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Secure Environment Templates
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request focused on configuration hygiene.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an environment variable template for staging and production. Mark secrets clearly and avoid real credentials or reusable default passwords.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Infrastructure Scaffold
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for cloud deployment preparation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft Terraform scaffolding for an AWS web application using VPC, RDS, ECS, and an application load balancer. Include variable and state guidance.

output_examples.input: I need local development files for a web app with a database and cache.
output_examples.output: A Docker Compose plan, environment variable checklist, startup commands, and notes for local service readiness.

output_examples.input: Help my team onboard contributors to our containerized project.
output_examples.output: A dev container outline, Makefile task list, project structure, and README sections for setup and troubleshooting.

output_examples.input: Prepare Terraform guidance for moving this service toward AWS.
output_examples.output: A resource plan covering provider setup, networking, database configuration, container services, load balancing, and sensitive variables.

best_practices: Replace all placeholder credentials before any shared or production deployment.
Keep real secrets in managed secret stores, not environment files or repository history.
Review generated infrastructure for least privilege, network exposure, backups, and state protection.
anti_patterns: Copying sample passwords into shared development or production systems.
Publishing environment files, Terraform state, or cloud credentials to a repository.
Opening database and cache ports beyond trusted local or private networks.

faq.question: Does this skill run Docker or Terraform for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup templates and commands that a user can review before running.

faq.question: Can the generated examples be used in production?
faq.answer: They need review before production use. Replace placeholders and validate networking, secrets, backups, and permissions.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows for environment setup guidance.

faq.question: Does it manage real credentials?
faq.answer: No. It describes environment variable names and placeholders, but real credentials should come from a secret manager.

faq.question: Can it support non-Node projects?
faq.answer: Yes, but prompts should specify the runtime, package manager, service ports, and required infrastructure.

faq.question: What should users review most carefully?
faq.answer: Users should review default passwords, exposed ports, Terraform state storage, and any cloud permissions.
